title: Repressing Gene Transcription by Redirecting Cellular Machinery with Chemical Epigenetic Modifiers
protocol: Grow fresh low-passage (less than passage 30) 293T human embryonic kidney cells in high-glucose DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 10 mM HEPES, 1x NEAA, Pen/Strep, and 2-mercaptoenthanol.
Split the cells every 3 to 5 days before they become >95% confluent.
Aspirate the old media from a 15-cm plate of 293T HEK cells.
Add 10 mL of 1x PBS and aspirate it.
Add 3 mL of 0.05% trypsin to the cells.
Incubate the cells in trypsin for 8 min at 37°C, rocking and tapping halfway through.
When cells reach 60-80% confluency, perform a PEI transfection with 13.5 µg of psPAX2 plasmid, 4.5 µg of pMD2.G plasmid, 18 µg of lentiviral-compatible delivery vector, and 108 µL of PEI.
Gently mix the DNA, PEI, and transfection media in a 15-mL conical tube.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 15 min.
Add the mixture dropwise to the 15-cm plate.
Aspirate the media after 16 h of transfection and incubation.
Add fresh 293 HEK media prewarmed in a 37°C water bath to the 15-cm plates.
Incubate cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 48 h after media change.
Grow low-passage CiA mESCs in high-glucose DMEM base media supplemented with required components.
Preincubate plates with 0.1% gelatin in 1x PBS for 1 - 3 h.
Wash plates with 1x PBS.
Feed cells daily and split them every 2 - 3 d as needed.
Passage mESC into a 12-well plate format (100,000 cells/well) 1 day prior to infection.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Aspirate the old media from cells grown in a 10-cm format.
Add 5 mL of 1x PBS and aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin to the cells.
Incubate the cells in trypsin at 37 °C for 8 min, rocking and tapping halfway through.
Remove and transfer the supernatant from 293T 15-cm viral packaging cells into a 50-mL conical tube after 48 h of media change.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 300 x g for 5 min to pellet cell debris.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45-µm SFCA membrane.
Concentrate the virus with ultracentrifugation using an SW32 rotor at 20,000 rpm (~72,000 x g) for 2.5 h at 4 °C.
Treat CiA mESCs in a 12-well plate with fresh ES media containing 5 µg/mL of polybrene.
Aspirate the supernatant and suspend the virus pellet in 100 μL of 1x PBS, avoiding excess bubbles.
Add the virus and 1x PBS to a 1.5-mL microfuge tube.
Vortex/shake the tube at 300 x g (or lowest setting) to fully suspend the virus.
Spin down the tube in a mini-tabletop centrifuge for 5 - 10 s to remove bubbles.
Add 30 µL of the virus to each well of a 12-well plate.
Swirl the plate and then centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 20 min.
Flash freeze the virus with liquid nitrogen and store it at -80 °C.
Place the 12-well plate back in the 37 °C incubator.
Change the media to fresh ES media following morning (~16 h later).
Select for cells that integrated the viral plasmid by adding an appropriate antibiotic after 48 h of infection.
Change the media daily and wash the cells with 1x PBS if a majority of the cells are floating/dead.
Keep the selection media on the cells for 72 - 96 h in a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2.
Suspend powdered CEM into dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to a stock concentration of 1 mM and a working concentration of 100 µM.
Split mESCs into a 12-well format with 100,000 cells/well after selection for 72 - 96 h.
Incubate the cells in a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Prepare a media solution of 100 nM CEM with ES media.
Feed the CiA mESC with 1 mL/well of the prepared media.
Keep a well of cells without any added CEMs as a control.
Aspirate old media from wells.
Add 1 mL/well of freshly prepared CEM-containing or CEM-free ES media.
Image cells without CEM treatment after 48 hours using a fluorescence microscope at 20X magnification.
Capture images under phase or brightfield for morphology recording.
Image both cell conditions under the FITC fluorescence channel.
Aspirate the media from control and CEM-treated cells.
Wash cells with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Add 0.25 mL of 0.25% trypsin with EDTA to cells.
Incubate for 8 - 10 min at room temperature.
Gently pipette up and down with a P1000 pipette if necessary.
Quench the trypsin with 1 mL of fresh media.
Resuspend cells in fresh media until in single-cell suspension.
Spin down cells at 300 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate supernatant.
Wash cells with 1x PBS and recentrifuge.
Aspirate PBS supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in FACS buffer.
Count the number of cells in three samples.
Average the concentration of cells.
Add more FACS buffer if needed to achieve a concentration between 1,000 - 3,000 cells/μL.
Perform flow cytometry on more than 50,000 cells while keeping them on ice.
Use a 530/40 filter for recording fluorescent changes.
Determine the appropriate voltage using an untreated control sample.
Set the voltage to place the fluorescent peak in the middle of the intensity spectrum.
Run samples at a sheath speed of around 5,000 cells/s.
Export flow cytometry data.
Analyze FCS files on a program such as FlowJo.
Gate first on forward scatter vs. side scatter for live cells.
Then gate on forward scatter height vs. area for singlets.
Visualize GFP channel data on a histogram to determine relative expression in targeted and control populations.
Split mESCs into a 10-cm plate with 3 million cells and 10 mL of ES media.
Add 10 mL of CEM-containing or CEM-free media the following day.
Aspirate old media after 48 hours of CEM treatment.
Wash and aspirate the cells with 5 mL of 1x PBS.
Dissociate the cells with 0.25% trypsin.
Quench the trypsin with 10 mL of ES media.
Count and isolate a sample of 10 million cells per condition.
Spin down each of the 10 million cell samples at 300 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend each pellet in 10 mL of 1x PBS.
Recentrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend each pellet in 10 mL of CiA Fix buffer.
Add 1 mL of 11% formaldehyde solution and immediately invert the samples 5x - 10x.
Incubate the sample at room temperature for 10 min.
Add 0.5 mL of 2.5 M glycine.
Invert the samples immediately and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of CiA Rinse 1.
Incubate the sample on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge it at 1,200 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of CiA Rinse 2.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Add 5 mL of CiA shearing buffer along the sides of the conical tube to wash off any salt without disrupting the pellet.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 x g for 3 min at 4 °C.
Repeat the wash step.
Resuspend the pellet in 90 µL of CiA shearing buffer and fresh protease inhibitors.
Add 10 µL of sonication-enhancing nanodroplets while keeping everything on ice.
Transfer 100 µL of the solution to a glass tube and cap the tube.
Sonicate the samples for 3.5 min at an acoustic power of 55 W.
Process the samples in 2-min-maximum cycle times if the total sonication time exceeds 2 min.
Transfer each sonicated chromatin sample to a new 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin the tubes at 8,000 x g for 2 min at 4 °C.
Determine DNA concentration spectrophotometrically.
Run approximately 200 ng of DNA on a 1% agarose gel to verify chromatin size.
Follow the ChIP kit manufacturer's protocol for immunoprecipitation and isolating chromatin.
Warm elution buffer at 37 °C for samples with higher DNA concentrations.
Elute samples twice with 30 µL of elution buffer, spinning for 1 min each time.
Load reagents into a 384-well plate for qPCR.
Add 5 μL of 2x asymmetrical cyanine dye master mix to the plate.
Add 2.5 μM of each primer set to the plate.
Add water and 0.1 - 10 ng of DNA for each reaction in the plate.
Design primers to amplify 50 - 100 bp amplicons.
Normalize CT values to a house-keeping gene, intracisternal A-type particles (IAP).
Run qPCR with 40 cycles at an annealing temperature of 60 °C for 1 min.
